cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset, saving 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms), per dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3. The Meridian 120 Hz mode's lowest preset is Ultra Performance, which Skiff does not use.

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. "Co-op rollback netcode prototype" was abandoned: rollback re-runs tides every frame, costing 4.8 ms on Skiff, so co-op will ship without it (dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). "Shader compile cache and build farm" was completed once every farm build read from the cache (fnd-retrospective-on-the-shader-compile-cache--9rpv2a60ach04cx6, which reports the cache running on every farm build with a 94% hit rate and clean rebuilds down from 47 minutes to 6 min 40 s).

netcode-004.answer: Rollback was abandoned because co-op needs bit-for-bit deterministic tides, and rollback must re-run the tide simulation every rolled-back frame, costing 4.8 ms on Skiff (a fifth of the 25 ms frame); the reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e (abandon decision: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b).

ports-012.answer: They raised the Skiff dynamic resolution floor to 576p because saltglass caustics shimmered badly at the 540p floor, even after Tern (visible in 7 of 10 dune views, versus 2 of 10 at 576p). See dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb, citing fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Alpha-tested foliage was moved out of the visibility buffer because it cost 2.1 ms there versus 0.8 ms in forward rendering, so it stays in a forward pass after the resolve; saltglass was moved out because it refracts the resolved scene and so needs that scene to be rendered first (record dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9).

render-032.answer: The team chose Tern because Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping it on two platforms would break the one-upscaler constraint; owning the code also mattered more for saltglass than raw quality, since the team can change Tern the same week without a vendor ticket or license (dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e).

render-046.answer: The cost finding that sank virtual shadow maps (3.1 ms) was a capture error; with cached pages, VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascades, so the sun decision was reopened (record dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4).

render-047.answer: Because a release-build capture showed the visibility buffer on Skiff at 7.4 ms versus 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so the forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month. Record: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired fibers for engine jobs because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack (fiber stacks made crash dumps unreadable), which blocked crash triage for beta, and fibers gained only about two points of utilisation (95% vs 93% for the continuation prototype) while also causing the Gull thread-local bug. Record: dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h

world-051.answer: Float tides drifted apart between machines, and strict IEEE flags fixed only the compiler, not Skiff's math library, whose sin() differs by one ulp (fnd-strict-float-mode-still-diverges-because-skiff-s--z811r28v0a1wzb13). Fixed-point 32.32 arithmetic uses only integer adds and multiplies plus a build-time sine table, so it gives identical bits on every CPU and compiler (dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e).

world-055.answer: Kelp stayed because the team shrank its dictionary to 1 MB, which beat Zstandard cold on Skiff (2.2 GB/s vs 1.3 GB/s, per the superseded finding), so the 4 MB dictionary's loss was fixed rather than abandoning Kelp; see dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew. Firmware 3.2 later cut the margin to 1.5 vs 1.2 GB/s, but Kelp still wins.
